Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted declaration cbrld_sphere_slice_isIntegerMultiplicity (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.lower_density-a1.slice-a1, candidate commit c226ea8f92107f43aeaa2e467c96b78f0c496960) with the identical frozen type (the declaration line at that commit is string-equal to this lean_statement); no new worker is needed. Its accepted proof is reproduced below.
Provenance in the present node: step 3 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2(1)–(2) and 4.9): for the cycle C, Z = ∂(C⌞B_ρ(x₁)) is integer multiplicity for a.e. ρ, is supported in ∂B_ρ(x₁), and its mass is bounded by the slice liminf of r ↦ μ(B_r(x₁)).
1. Let f(x) := dist(x, x₁) = |x − x₁|. f is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.dist_left), {x : f(x) < t} = B_t(x₁) and {x : t − h < f(x) < t} = {x : t − h < |x − x₁| < t}. Let μ' := 0 (the zero measure) and ξ' := 0 (the zero field of d-vectors). Then (μ', ξ') is an admissible representation of ∂C = 0: μ' is finite on compacts, ξ' is strongly measurable, |ξ'(x)(α)| = 0 ≤ |α|, and ∂C(η) = 0 = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for every test form η.

2. Apply the ISP hypothesis of C to the representations (μ, ξ) of C and (μ', ξ') of ∂C, to f and to L = 1: for L¹-a.e. t, for all currents A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) and B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms, ∂A − B is integer multiplicity. Let N be the set of t ∈ ℝ at which this property fails; by ae_iff, N is Lebesgue-null.

3. Apply (SL) with k := d, U := ℝ^P (open), T := C, the representations (μ, ξ) and (μ', ξ'), f and L := 1; all its hypotheses hold (finiteness on compacts, measurability, the pointwise bounds, the representations of C and of ∂C from step 1, f Lipschitz). This gives currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P), t ∈ ℝ, with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η)dμ' = 0 (an integral against the zero measure), ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅, and M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ 1·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open W.

4. Fix ρ > 0 with ρ ∉ N and put A := A_ρ. Then A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x₁)} ξ(ω)dμ for every test form ω. All values of B_ρ vanish, so B_ρ = 0 and ∂A − B_ρ = ∂A (extensionality of currents).

5. (Integer multiplicity.) Since ρ ∉ N, the property of step 2 holds at t = ρ; applied to A_ρ and B_ρ, whose values are given by the formulas of step 3, it shows that ∂A − B_ρ = ∂A is integer multiplicity.

6. (Support.) Let y ∈ ℝ^P with y ∉ ∂B_ρ(x₁), let r := |dist(y, x₁) − ρ|/2 > 0 and W' := B_r(y), an open set whose closure B̄_r(y) is compact. For z ∈ W', |dist(z, x₁) − dist(y, x₁)| ≤ |z − y| < r < |dist(y, x₁) − ρ|, so dist(z, x₁) ≠ ρ; hence every test form η with tsupport η ⊆ W' satisfies tsupport η ∩ {f = ρ} = ∅ and therefore ∂A(η) = B_ρ(η) = 0 by step 3. Thus ∂A vanishes on W', so W' is contained in the zero region of ∂A and y ∉ spt ∂A. Hence spt ∂A ⊆ ∂B_ρ(x₁).

7. (Mass.) Step 3 with the open set W := ℝ^P gives M(∂A) = M_{ℝ^P}(∂A − B_ρ) ≤ 1·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(ℝ^P ∩ {ρ − h < f < ρ}) = liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ({x : ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}) (the factor (1 : ℝ≥0) cast to [0, ∞] is 1, and ℝ^P ∩ X = X). ∎
proof_key_steps: Slice by the 1-Lipschitz f = |· − x₁|, representing ∂C = 0 by the zero measure and zero field.
ISP yields a Lebesgue-null set N outside of which ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity.
(SL) gives A_t = C⌞{f < t}, B_t = 0, the vanishing of ∂A_t off {f = t} and the liminf mass bound.
For ρ ∉ N: ∂A_ρ is integer multiplicity, spt ∂A_ρ ⊆ ∂B_ρ(x₁), and M(∂A_ρ) ≤ liminf_h h⁻¹μ{ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}.

Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted declaration cbrld_exists_good_slice_radius (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.lower_density-a1.radius-a1, candidate commit 215074ec7e0fa6a1701b78cbd48d0787bad62d32) with the identical frozen type (the declaration line at that commit is string-equal to this lean_statement); no new worker is needed. Its accepted proof is reproduced below.
Provenance in the present node: step 2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2(2)–(3)): since ∫_0^s (F^{1/n})' ≤ F(s)^{1/n} < as, a positive-measure set of radii has (F^{1/n})' ≤ 2a; off null sets this gives F' = nF^{(n−1)/n}(F^{1/n})' ≤ 2naF^{(n−1)/n} and μ(∂B_ρ(x₁)) = 0.
1. For r ∈ ℝ let F(r) := μ(B_r(x₁)), a finite real number (B_r(x₁) ⊆ B̄_r(x₁), which is compact). F is nondecreasing and F(r) = 0 for r ≤ 0 (the ball is empty). Let G(r) := F(r)^{1/n} (real power of a nonnegative number); G is nondecreasing, G(r) = 0 for r ≤ 0, and G(r)^n = F(r) for every r (Real.rpow_inv_natCast_pow, n ≥ 1).

2. From μ(B_s(x₁)) < (as)^n we get F(s) < (as)^n and hence G(s) < as, because u ↦ u^{1/n} is strictly increasing on [0, ∞) and as > 0.

3. Let G' := deriv G (equal to 0 where G is not differentiable); G' ≥ 0 everywhere (Monotone.deriv_nonneg). Since G is monotone on [0, s], Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv and MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc show that G' is integrable on [0, s] and ∫_0^s G' ≤ G(s) − G(0) = G(s) < as.

4. Let E := {r ∈ (0, s) : G'(r) ≤ 2a}; it is measurable (deriv G is measurable, measurable_deriv). E has positive Lebesgue measure: otherwise G'(r) > 2a for a.e. r ∈ (0, s), and then ∫_0^s G' ≥ ∫_0^s 2a = 2as > as, contradicting step 3.

5. The following sets are Lebesgue-null: N (by hypothesis); D := {r : G is not differentiable at r} (Lebesgue's theorem for monotone functions, Mathlib Monotone.ae_differentiableAt); and Q := {r : μ(∂B_r(x₁)) > 0}, which is countable because the spheres ∂B_r(x₁), r ∈ ℝ, are pairwise disjoint closed (measurable) sets and μ is σ-finite (ℝ^P is a countable union of compact balls of finite μ-measure; Mathlib Measure.countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion, whose SFinite instance is obtained by registering IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ from the hypothesis). Since E has positive measure, E ⊄ N ∪ D ∪ Q; choose ρ ∈ E ∖ (N ∪ D ∪ Q). Then 0 < ρ < s, ρ ∉ N, μ(∂B_ρ(x₁)) = 0, G is differentiable at ρ and G'(ρ) ≤ 2a.

6. Since F = G^n, F is differentiable at ρ with F'(ρ) = n·G(ρ)^{n−1}·G'(ρ) ≤ 2na·G(ρ)^{n−1} = 2na·F(ρ)^{(n−1)/n}, because G(ρ) ≥ 0 and G(ρ)^{n−1} = (F(ρ)^{1/n})^{n−1} = F(ρ)^{(n−1)/n}.

Source: steps 2–4 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2(2)–(4), with the parent's corrections: the lower density replaces Θ^{*n}, and the support of the filling is controlled by the support bound of the isoperimetric filling). The argument is the accepted proof of cbrld_exists_small_filling_of_low_density (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.lower_density-a1.local_filling-a1, candidate commit 348cc6f616fa56dce61ca9cf76278330359db2c3) with exactly one change: the filling is taken from the in-range hypothesis (Isor) instead of the unrestricted (ISO), and (Isor) is applied only at (P, m) with d = m + 1, where m + 1 = d < d + 1 < P. Siblings used: small_scale (steps 1–2), slice and radius (step 3), mass_gap (step 5), constants (step 6).

Notation: n := d + 1 ≥ 1; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ [0, ∞] and w := ω_n read as a real number; for a current Z, M(Z) := Z.mass = M_{ℝ^P}(Z) ∈ [0, ∞]; powers with real exponents are Real.rpow, with (n − 1)/n computed in ℝ from the cast of n.

1. (Reduction to a filling constant.) Fix P, d with d + 1 < P. It suffices to find a real a > 0, depending only on P and d, with the property
(H) for all x₁ ∈ ℝ^P, reals δ, s, ρ, F and A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with 0 < s, ρ < s, s < δ, 0 ≤ F ≤ (as)^n, ∂A integer multiplicity, spt ∂A ⊆ ∂B_ρ(x₁) and M(∂A) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(2na·F^{(n−1)/n}), there is S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂S = ∂A, M(S) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(F/2) and spt S ⊆ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x₁).
Indeed, suppose a > 0 has (H). Sibling small_scale, part (a) for n, gives w > 0. Put η₀ := a^n/w > 0. Fix C, μ, ξ satisfying the hypotheses of the statement (∂C = 0, μ finite on compacts, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e., C(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, ISP), a point x₁ with liminf_{r↓0} μ(B_r(x₁))/(ω_n r^n) < ENNReal.ofReal η₀, and δ > 0. Steps 2–4 produce ρ, A, S as required.

2. (Small scale.) Sibling small_scale, part (b) with P, μ, x₁, η₀ and δ, gives s with 0 < s < δ and μ(B_s(x₁)) < ENNReal.ofReal(η₀·w·s^n). Since η₀·w = a^n (w ≠ 0) and a^n·s^n = (as)^n, μ(B_s(x₁)) < ENNReal.ofReal((as)^n).

3. (Good radius and slice.) Sibling slice (with (SL), P, d, C, μ, ξ, x₁, ∂C = 0, the representation hypotheses and ISP) gives a Lebesgue-null set N ⊆ ℝ. Sibling radius (with P, n, μ, x₁, a, s and N; μ finite on compacts, 1 ≤ n, a > 0, s > 0, the bound of step 2 and volume N = 0) gives ρ with 0 < ρ < s, ρ ∉ N, μ(∂B_ρ(x₁)) = 0 and ℓ := liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹·μ({x : ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(2na·F^{(n−1)/n}), where F := μ(B_ρ(x₁)) read as a real number. The conclusion of slice at ρ (ρ > 0, ρ ∉ N) gives A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x₁)} ξ(ω)dμ for every test form ω, ∂A integer multiplicity, spt ∂A ⊆ ∂B_ρ(x₁) and M(∂A) ≤ ℓ, hence M(∂A) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(2na·F^{(n−1)/n}). Since B_ρ(x₁) ⊆ B_s(x₁), μ(B_ρ(x₁)) ≤ μ(B_s(x₁)) < ENNReal.ofReal((as)^n) < ∞; so μ(B_ρ(x₁)) is finite, F ≥ 0, and F ≤ (as)^n (ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal, using (as)^n ≥ 0).

4. (Conclusion from (H).) Apply (H) to x₁, δ, s, ρ, F and A (0 < s, ρ < s < δ, 0 ≤ F ≤ (as)^n and the properties of ∂A from step 3). It gives S with ∂S = ∂A, M(S) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(F/2) and spt S ⊆ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x₁). Since μ(B_ρ(x₁)) < ∞, ENNReal.ofReal(F/2) = ENNReal.ofReal((1/2)·F) = ENNReal.ofReal(1/2)·ENNReal.ofReal(F) = ENNReal.ofReal(1/2)·μ(B_ρ(x₁)) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with 1/2 ≥ 0, then ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). Together with 0 < ρ < s < δ and μ(∂B_ρ(x₁)) = 0, the radius ρ and the currents A, S satisfy every requirement of the conclusion. It remains to produce a with (H); we distinguish d = 0 and d = m + 1.

5. (Case d = 0, n = 1.) Take a := 1/4 > 0. In (H), (n − 1)/n = 0, so F^{(n−1)/n} = F^0 = 1 and 2na·F^{(n−1)/n} = 2·1·(1/4)·1 = 1/2; hence M(∂A) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(1/2) < 1. As ∂A ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, sibling mass_gap (with (MR)) gives ∂A = 0. Take S := 0 ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P). Then ∂S = 0 = ∂A (extensionality: (∂0)(η) = 0(dη) = 0 for every η). M(S) = 0 ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(F/2), because every value of the zero current is 0, so the supremum defining M(0) is 0. And spt S = ∅ ⊆ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x₁): every y ∈ ℝ^P lies in the open ball B_1(y), an open set with compact closure on which the zero current vanishes, so y lies in the zero region of 0.

6. (Case d = m + 1, n = m + 2.) From d + 1 < P we get m + 1 < P, so (Isor) at (P, m) gives a real c ≥ 1 such that every integer multiplicity Z ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with compact support, ∂Z = 0 and M(Z) < ∞ equals ∂Y for some integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with M(Y) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(c(2cM)^{1/(m+1)}M) and spt Y ⊆ thickening(3√P(2cM)^{1/(m+1)}, spt Z), where M := M(Z) read as a real number. Sibling constants, with m and c ≥ 1, gives a > 0 such that for all reals s, F, M with s ≥ 0, F ≥ 0, F ≤ (as)^{m+2} and 0 ≤ M ≤ 2n·a·F^{(n−1)/n}: (A) c(2cM)^{1/(m+1)}M ≤ F/2 and (B) (2cM)^{1/(m+1)} ≤ s. We verify (H) for this a. Let x₁, δ, s, ρ, F and A be as in (H), and Z := ∂A ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P).
(a) ∂Z = ∂∂A = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary); Z is integer multiplicity by assumption; spt Z is closed, being the complement of the open zero region of Z, and is contained in the compact sphere ∂B_ρ(x₁), hence compact; and M(Z) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(2na·F^{(n−1)/n}) < ∞.
(b) (Isor) gives Y as above. Put M := M(Z) read as a real number. Since 2na·F^{(n−1)/n} ≥ 0, M(Z) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(2na·F^{(n−1)/n}) gives 0 ≤ M ≤ 2na·F^{(n−1)/n} (ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal). Sibling constants, applied with s (s ≥ 0 because s > 0), F (0 ≤ F ≤ (as)^{m+2}) and M, gives (A) and (B).
(c) Take S := Y. Then ∂S = Z = ∂A, and M(S) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(c(2cM)^{1/(m+1)}M) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(F/2) by (A) and monotonicity of ENNReal.ofReal.
(d) Let y ∈ spt S. By the support bound of (Isor) and Metric.mem_thickening_iff there is z ∈ spt Z with |y − z| < 3√P(2cM)^{1/(m+1)}. By (B) and s < δ, (2cM)^{1/(m+1)} ≤ s ≤ δ, so 3√P(2cM)^{1/(m+1)} ≤ 3√P·δ (√P ≥ 0). Since spt Z ⊆ ∂B_ρ(x₁), |z − x₁| = ρ < s < δ. By the triangle inequality |y − x₁| ≤ |y − z| + |z − x₁| < 3√P·δ + δ = (1 + 3√P)δ, so y ∈ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x₁). Hence spt S ⊆ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x₁).

7. (Conclusion.) In both cases a > 0 has (H), so by steps 1–4 the number η₀ = a^n/w > 0, which depends only on P and d (through c of (Isor) at (P, d − 1) when d ≥ 1), has the asserted property. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to a constant a > 0 with the slice-filling property (H) and put η₀ := a^n/ω_n (small_scale gives ω_n > 0).
small_scale gives s ∈ (0, δ) with μ(B_s(x₁)) < (as)^n.

slice gives a null set N; radius gives ρ ∈ (0, s) ∖ N with μ(∂B_ρ(x₁)) = 0 and slice liminf ≤ 2naF^{(n−1)/n}; slice at ρ gives A = C⌞B_ρ(x₁) with ∂A integer multiplicity on the sphere and M(∂A) ≤ 2naF^{(n−1)/n}.
n = 1: a = 1/4, so M(∂A) ≤ 1/2 < 1, ∂A = 0 by mass_gap, and S = 0.
n = m + 2: (Isor) at (P, m), m + 1 = d < P, fills Z = ∂A by S; constants gives M(S) ≤ F/2 and filling radius ≤ s, so spt S ⊆ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x₁).
Convert M(S) ≤ ofReal(F/2) into M(S) ≤ ½·μ(B_ρ(x₁)) using μ(B_ρ(x₁)) < ∞.

Let P, d ∈ ℕ, C ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), μ a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K and μ(W) = M_W(C) for every open W, ξ a μ-a.e. strongly measurable field of (d+1)-vectors with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and all α, with C(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ for every test form ω. Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted declaration cbrld_measure_eq_zero_of_small_fillings (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.lower_density-a1.null_set-a1, candidate commit b6539fa1429757b85cc062fc80420150d5b919ee) with the identical frozen type (the declaration line at that commit is string-equal to this lean_statement); no new worker is needed. Its accepted proof is given below in condensed, restructured form, with the two auxiliary accepted results it uses proved inline. The argument is the accepted proof (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2(4)–(6), corrected) of the parent's steps 0, 5 and 6, carried out for each admissible test form separately: for a W-admissible ω, C(ω) is bounded through the comparison cycles X = S − C⌞B_ρ(x), which is the estimate behind M_W(C_δ) ≤ μ(W ∖ ⋃B_i) + κΣμ(B_i) and C_δ ⇀ C; taking the supremum over ω replaces lower semicontinuity, and the Borel measurability of the density (parent step 1) is not needed because E is arbitrary. The two accepted auxiliary results used by the accepted Lean proof, the cone inequality cbrld_cycle_eval_le_radius_mul_mass and the covering estimate cbrld_vitali_setIntegral_le, are proved in steps 2 and 3. (λ denotes the Lean variable lam.)

Notation: n := d + 1; |β| := covectorEuclideanNorm β, the Euclidean norm of the coefficients β(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)}) over increasing multi-indices I; a test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) is G-admissible if tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; M_G(T) = sup{max(T(ω), 0) : ω G-admissible} (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn); M := M_{ℝ^P}; masses and measures are read as real numbers when finite.

1. (Elementary facts.) For S, A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P):
(a) (S − A)(ω) = S(ω) − A(ω), and ∂(S − A) = ∂S − ∂A, since ∂(S − A)(η) = (S − A)(dη) = S(dη) − A(dη) (extensionality of currents).
(b) |tβ| = |t|·|β| for t ∈ ℝ (each coefficient scales by t); in particular |−β| = |β|.
(c) If M(T) < ∞, φ is a test form and s ≥ 0 with |φ(x)| ≤ s for all x, then |T(φ)| ≤ s·M(T): for every t > s the forms ±t⁻¹φ are ℝ^P-admissible by (b), so ±t⁻¹T(φ) = T(±t⁻¹φ) ≤ M(T) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn), i.e. |T(φ)| ≤ t·M(T); let t ↓ s.
(d) M(S − A) ≤ M(S) + M(A): for ℝ^P-admissible ω, (S − A)(ω) = S(ω) + A(−ω) and max(S(ω) + A(−ω), 0) ≤ max(S(ω), 0) + max(A(−ω), 0) ≤ M(S) + M(A) (−ω is admissible by (b)); take the supremum.
(e) spt(S − A) ⊆ spt S ∪ spt A: if y ∉ spt S ∪ spt A there are open W₁, W₂ ∋ y with compact closures on which S resp. A vanish (on test forms supported there); S − A vanishes on W₁ ∩ W₂, so y is in the zero region of S − A.
(f) If A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ξ(ω)dμ for all ω, then M(A) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)) and spt A ⊆ B̄_ρ(x). For ℝ^P-admissible ω, |ξ(y)(ω(y))| ≤ |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for μ-a.e. y, so A(ω) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)) (finite, as B̄_ρ(x) is compact); take the supremum. If y ∉ B̄_ρ(x), put r := (|y − x| − ρ)/2 > 0; the ball B_r(y) is open with compact closure and disjoint from B_ρ(x), so every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B_r(y) vanishes on B_ρ(x) and A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ξ(y)(0)dμ = 0; hence y ∉ spt A.

2. (Cone inequality; accepted cbrld_cycle_eval_le_radius_mul_mass.) For every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) there is c ≥ 0 such that |X(ω)| ≤ c·ϱ·M(X) for every X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂X = 0 and M(X) < ∞, every x₀ ∈ ℝ^P and every ϱ > 0 with spt X ⊆ B̄_ϱ(x₀).
(i) (Constant.) ω is smooth with compact support, so its derivative Dω is continuous with compact support, hence bounded by some L₀ ≥ 0; by the mean value inequality on the convex set ℝ^P, ‖ω(x) − ω(y)‖ ≤ L₀|x − y| (operator norm). Each coefficient of a k-covector β is bounded by ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm on unit vectors) and there are at most P^n index maps, so |β| ≤ P^{n/2}‖β‖. Put c := P^{n/2}L₀; then |ω(x) − ω(y)| ≤ c|x − y| for all x, y, and c depends only on ω.
(ii) (Cut-off.) Fix X, x₀, ϱ as above and ε > 0. Let ζ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] be a smooth bump (ContDiffBump) with ζ = 1 on B̄_{ϱ+ε/2}(x₀) and ζ(x) = 0 for |x − x₀| ≥ ϱ + ε, and G := B_{ϱ+ε/2}(x₀) ⊇ B̄_ϱ(x₀) ⊇ spt X. For every test form φ, (1 − ζ)φ is a test form vanishing on the open set G, so its topological support lies in ℝ^P ∖ G and is disjoint from spt X; by (VO), X((1 − ζ)φ) = 0, hence X(φ) = X(ζφ).
(iii) (Constant forms.) Let α := ω(x₀) ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P) and ψ(x) := n⁻¹·α.curryLeft(x − x₀), the (n−1)-form ψ(x)(v₁, …, v_{n−1}) = n⁻¹·α(x − x₀, v₁, …, v_{n−1}). ψ is affine with Dψ(x) = n⁻¹·α.curryLeft, so dψ(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(n⁻¹·α.curryLeft) = n⁻¹·(n • α) = α for every x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft). ζψ is a test form, and on G, ζψ = ψ, so d(ζψ) = α = ζα there (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq). Thus the test form ζα − d(ζψ) vanishes on G, (VO) gives X(ζα − d(ζψ)) = 0, and X(d(ζψ)) = ∂X(ζψ) = 0 because ∂X = 0. Hence X(ζα) = 0.

Proof. μ is finite on the compact balls B̄_k(0), hence σ-finite (s-finite) and locally finite, and g is integrable on every measurable set of finite measure. For x ∈ ℝ^P let f(x) be the set of ρ > 0 with B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ W and ∫_{B̄_ρ(x)} g dμ ≤ θμ(B̄_ρ(x)); since W is open, the hypothesis applied below a radius r with B_r(x) ⊆ W shows that f(x) meets (0, δ) for every x ∈ E' and δ > 0. Besicovitch.exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae (ℝ^P has the Besicovitch covering property) gives a countable t ⊆ E' and r(x) ∈ f(x), x ∈ t, such that the closed balls B_x := B̄_{r(x)}(x) are pairwise disjoint and μ(E' ∖ V) = 0 for V := ⋃_{x∈t} B_x. V is measurable, V ⊆ W, μ(V) ≤ μ(W) < ∞ and μ(E') ≤ μ(V) + μ(E' ∖ V) = μ(V). By countable additivity, μ(V) = Σ_x μ(B_x) and ∫_V g dμ = Σ_x ∫_{B_x} g dμ ≤ θΣ_x μ(B_x) = θμ(V). Since g ≤ 1 a.e., ∫_{W∖V} g dμ ≤ μ(W ∖ V) = μ(W) − μ(V). Adding, ∫_W g dμ ≤ μ(W) − (1 − θ)μ(V) ≤ μ(W) − (1 − θ)μ(E'), because 1 − θ ≥ 0.
